Rafael —

Thanks for sharing. Quick read from our side: procurement is generally OK with the commercial terms, but legal/marketing have concerns about the publicity and reference carve-outs. High-level feedback: 

1) "Right to use logo and customer name" — we need this to be strictly optional and subject to an approval process; we cannot grant blanket, perpetual rights.
2) Case studies — we need a clear approval window (we prefer 10 business days) and the right to redact any customer-identifiable data.
3) Testimonials/quotes — must be attributed and pre-approved; no implied endorsement language.
4) Embargo — ClearSight requires 10 business days prior notice for any joint announcement during the first 12 months post-launch.

I've looped Tom (marketing lead) — he can confirm whether marketing will allow the logo asset in a customer carousel (likely yes, with the approval flow).

If you want to expedite, I can introduce our outside counsel (Meghan O'Neill) to your legal team and we can do a one-hour call to resolve the publicity clauses.

Rafael / Camila —

Thanks for forwarding. I reviewed the redline and Sara's note. Below is a short summary and proposed compromise language we typically use for enterprise customers who want tighter controls. If you want, I can prepare a tracked-change doc to send to Meghan.

Summary of compromise approach:
- Logo/name: Customer grants the right to include Customer's name and logo in Redwood's marketing materials only with prior written approval of a representative designated by Customer for each use. Approval to be provided within ten (10) business days of request; failure to respond constitutes approval only if Customer explicitly opts into an automatic approval flow (not default).
- Case study & quotes: Any case study, quote, or testimonial will be subject to Customer review and final written approval; Customer may request redaction of Customer-identifiable data and may decline to include specific metrics.
- Embargo and announcements: The Parties will coordinate any public announcement and provide at least ten (10) business days' notice. For the first twelve (12) months following execution, Customer may require Redwood to delay publication.
- Limited perpetual usage: For references (e.g., inclusion in a customer list), the license is non-exclusive, revocable on thirty (30) days' notice if Customer reasonably determines continued use is harmful.

Proposed short clause (to paste into MSA):
"Publicity and References. Customer consents to (i) the inclusion of Customer's name and logo in Redwood's marketing materials and customer lists, and (ii) the use of short, pre-approved quotes or case studies (each, a \"Reference\") subject to Customer's prior written approval, which Customer shall not unreasonably withhold or delay and which Customer shall provide or withhold within ten (10) business days of receipt of a request. Customer may redact or remove customer-identifiable data from any Reference. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may revoke permission for any future Reference upon thirty (30) days' written notice to Redwood. All References shall be used in accordance with Customer's published brand guidelines and with no implication of endorsement beyond the factual statement of a business relationship"

I attached a short doc with the tracked language: publicity_clause_suggestion.docx.

If that language is acceptable, Rafael, please propose it to Meghan and Sara. If Meghan wants edits, we can host a 30–45 minute call to resolve final wording; having both counsels on the call tends to speed things up.
